name: DGX Spark Inkling 2 Mini Atlas (SparkInkling 0.4.2)

weights.description: Which weights the engine serves: strict is the checkpoint as shipped; spark adds SparkInkling's calibrated NVFP4 overlay for decode.

strict.description: Thinking Machines' checkpoint as shipped (NVFP4 experts in layers 0-19, MXFP8 in 20-23, BF16 attention, router and vocabulary head).

spark.description: Strict plus Enntity/Inkling-2-Mini-Spark-NVFP4 (2.9 GB): calibrated NVFP4 attention projections, vocabulary head and layer 20-23 experts. Next-token KL 0.0081 to Strict on 224 held-out documents (97.0% top-1 agreement).

summary: Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini on one DGX Spark with SparkInkling 0.4.2's Atlas build: the checkpoint's own DSpark drafter, prefix caching, up to 131072-token requests (262144 in the max mode). --weights strict (default) serves the checkpoint as shipped; --weights spark adds a calibrated NVFP4 overlay. Three modes: default (8 requests), saver (8 requests at half the GPU memory) and max (32 requests). Additive only: no default model, no aliases.
description: This recipe installs SparkInkling 0.4.2 at the immutable product revision recorded in backends/atlas-sparkinkling/pins-0.4.2.json. The Atlas engine image is built from Enntity/sparkinkling by install/build.sh and published to GHCR; LLooM commits no engine source. Setup acquires thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini (and, with --weights spark, Enntity/Inkling-2-Mini-Spark-NVFP4, sha256-checked) at pinned revisions, pulls the image by its manifest digest and verifies it, then runs SparkInkling's own install/check_files.py, dspark_drafter.py and spark_overlay.py, fetched at the pinned revision, digest-checked and run inside the image with no network: they check the checkpoint's and overlay's weights against their pinned sha256, assemble the DSpark drafter directory and, with --weights spark, the Spark model directory beside the checkpoint. Setup remembers the weights it installed with.

provenance.source: SparkInkling 0.4.2: Enntity/sparkinkling 27e42a6f893cb4c38491e440b82d253c90548e98 (tag v0.4.2, install tree b1e18bf91437bd668926d853502e273253953310), engine Enntity/atlas inkling2/concurrent-spec-20261123 @ d3318e087850d59a05788bc89da749181e1bb289 (AGPL-3.0-only, recorded in the image's /opt/atlas/source-manifest.json). Image ghcr.io/enntity/atlas-sparkinkling:b1e18bf91437 (also :0.4.2), addressed by its GHCR manifest digest. Profiles default.json (0.80 GPU memory utilization, 8 sequences, 131072 tokens), saver.json (0.50, 8, 131072) and max.json (0.85, 32, 262144), all with BF16 KV, 4096-token prefill chunks and prefix caching. Model thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini revision ed40e7da625f594fc9c4990f5f66be24873c22d7 (Apache-2.0) with its bundled DSpark drafter; overlay Enntity/Inkling-2-Mini-Spark-NVFP4 @ e9df93dceea2fbf0927caf178104e868452a6292 (Apache-2.0).

hardware.testedMachine: One DGX Spark with 128 GB unified memory
notes: This version pins the SparkInkling 0.4.2 image (engine d3318e087). New since 0.4.1: tool-call arguments stream only to a request that sends stream_tool_arguments: true; every other request's calls are held until the tool guard (stream, the image's default) passes them, so a client that does not read the finish reason never receives a blocked call (in 0.4.1 every request's calls streamed). A verify stops where the drafter is unsure (the engine learns while serving how often each draft confidence is accepted); a sequence whose drafts stop paying decodes plainly for 32 tokens at first, doubling while re-probes fail, in place of the engine's throughput gate; Strict drafts two tokens each for two live requests; a verify attends exactly as decode does, so greedy text with drafts matched text without them in the release's checks; decode batches run at their own width; a Spark decode row's input projections run as one launch. Version 1 (SparkInkling 0.4.1) stays installable by number.

SparkInkling 0.4.2 on one GB10, 2026-11-23, RigMark protocol 1.1.0 (low reasoning effort, temperature 0), default profile and DSpark drafter, nothing else serving. Strict: code 65.2, prose 35.3, structured 92.6 tok/s, cold 32K prefill 3,274 tok/s, short code C1 / C2 / C4 / C8 41.3 / 63.1 / 85.0 / 120.7. Spark: code 77.5, prose 55.7, structured 103.6 tok/s, cold 32K prefill 3,277 tok/s, short code 53.9 / 77.7 / 105.8 / 135.4. Against 0.4.1: Strict code +20% and structured +16%, Spark code +13%; prose, prefill and four to eight requests level. Six of six output gates in both modes. Receipts: Enntity/sparkinkling results/2026-11-23-release-0.4.2.

Against vLLM's own Inkling 2 Mini image on the same Spark and protocol (measured 2026-11-20): vLLM without speculation read code 35.1, prose 35.6, 32K prefill 2,722, short code 35.1 / 54.0 / 86.6 / 122.4; with its DSpark drafter code 69.8, prose 31.2, structured 104.3, short code 43.4 / 60.9 / 94.7 / 144.0. Spark leads vLLM without speculation in every cell and vLLM with its drafter on code (1.11x), prose (1.78x), prefill (1.20x) and one to four requests, is level on structured output (0.99x) and trails at eight requests (0.94x). Strict leads vLLM without speculation on code (1.86x), structured output, prefill and one and two requests, and is within 1-2% on prose and at four and eight.

The 0.4.2 image build ran the engine's CPU workspace suite (8,819 tests passed) and Clippy. On the image, in both modes: a task probe (30 arithmetic word problems, 10 single-tool calls) passed 30/30 and 10/10; tool calls came back as calls blocking and streamed, with thinking on and off and with a forced tool choice; a call to a blocked address, asked for streamed, streamed and finished content_filter, and the same call not asked for streamed sent no arguments; an invoice image was transcribed exactly and a 3x3 labelled colour grid read 9/9. Smoke-level checks, not a qualification.
The DSpark drafter speculates for one live request in both modes and for two in Strict (two drafts each), and only while its drafts pay; from three requests the engine decodes plainly.

Profiles: default 8 requests of up to 131,072 tokens at 0.80 GPU memory utilization (a KV pool of about 404K tokens); saver 8 x 131,072 at 0.50 (212,672 tokens on the development build, where 8 concurrent short code requests all stopped normally); max 32 x 262,144 at 0.85 (about 446K tokens, so long requests wait for blocks). Requests the pool cannot hold yet wait rather than fail. The max profile was checked at 0.88 (32 concurrent short code requests all stopped normally, and a code hidden in a 182,100-token prompt was recalled), where the host kept about 8 GB available under the full batch; it ships at 0.85.

Peak host memory was not measured per mode. LLooM reserves an estimate: saver 66 GB, default 104 GB, max 110 GB. The container is capped at 114 GiB because a GB10 that runs out of shared memory hangs instead of killing a process. In the default and max modes little else should use this Spark's GPU memory.

The engine serves 127.0.0.1:8895 (fixed by the image) with host networking. Text and image input (OpenAI image_url parts with base64 data URIs; one image token per 40x40 pixel tile, no resize); no video.

Licenses: the Atlas engine and SparkInkling's install tools run from the image and are AGPL-3.0-only (not included in LLooM). thinkingmachines/Inkling-2-Mini and Enntity/Inkling-2-Mini-Spark-NVFP4 are Apache-2.0; the overlay's README is kept beside its weights for attribution.
